summary: Rosina Pastore is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She worked as an assistant and PhD candidate at Lausanne and is an Affiliated Researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Roy Rappaport was an anthropologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his doctorate from Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Tel Aviv University (~1998–2005) and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2005–2011) under Gary A. Tubb. He took up a post at Tel Aviv University around 2011.

Roy W. Perrett is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago (~1980–1984). He held posts at Massey University (~1987–2004), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2001–2011), and the University of Melbourne.

Royall Tyler is a Japanologist who earned his B.A. from Harvard and his master's and PhD from Columbia under Donald Keene (~1966–1977). He held teaching posts at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, Harvard, and headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and held an academic post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, later holding posts at Sophia (~1978–1989), Southern Methodist University (1989), and Ryukoku University.

Rudolf G. Wagner was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Bonn, Munich, Paris, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (~1972–1987) and Heidelberg University (~1987–2019), including its Cluster of Excellence (~2007–2012).

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history who studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium, the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1839), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1841–1843). He held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn. He held teaching posts in Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt and served as an academic councilor at Bonn (1974–2004).
Rudolf Lange was a scholar of Japanology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1922).
Rudolf Much was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Vienna (~1882–1887) and later held an academic post there (~1900–1934).

Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1888–1891) and under Richard von Garbe. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).
Rudolf Seydel was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Leipzig University (~1852–1856) and later held an academic post there (~1860–1892).

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University (~1877–1879) and under Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1898), the University of Freiburg (~1898–1913), and the University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift (~1839–1843) under Heinrich Ewald and in Paris under Eugène Burnouf. He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent from 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist educated at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Pathashala (1912–1918) and Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929).

Ruixuan Chen works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen completed a PhD at Leiden University (attested 2018) under Paul Harrison, with earlier study under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and holds a faculty post at Peking University (attested 2026).

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology who studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942). He held an academic post at Yale University from ~1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. He held positions at the University of Bristol from 1987, the Pali Text Society, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.
